# RIPS Law Librarian Blog

> A professional blog exploring trends in legal research, instruction, and patron services within modern law libraries, with focus on information access, technology adoption, and critical thinking in legal education.

RIPS Law Librarian Blog serves the law library community by publishing peer-reviewed and guest articles on emerging issues in legal librarianship, government information access, and information literacy. The blog features contributions from practicing law librarians and covers topics ranging from AI adoption and deepfakes to information literacy pedagogy and government transparency.

## Key Topics

- Information literacy
- Legal research
- Government transparency
- Generative AI
- Law librarianship
- Information access
- Deepfakes and evidence
- Boolean search
- Legal education
- Public information
- Intellectual freedom
- Research skills
- Professional development
- Academic libraries

## About & Leadership

- [RIPS Law Librarian Blog](https://ripslawlibrarian.wordpress.com): Homepage covering trends in law library research, instruction, and patron services.
- [Editors & Contributors](https://ripslawlibrarian.wordpress.com/blog-editor-contributors): Editor and contributor directory with contact information for blog submissions.
- [Executive Board](https://ripslawlibrarian.wordpress.com/executiveboard): RIPS executive board leadership and organizational structure with member details.

## Government Information & Access to Information Crisis

- [The Access to Information Crisis](https://ripslawlibrarian.wordpress.com/2025/03/12/the-access-to-information-crisis): Jennifer Chapman examines access to information crisis and First Amendment implications.
- [Finding the Unfindable in an Access to Information Crisis](https://ripslawlibrarian.wordpress.com/2025/04/16/finding-the-unfindable-in-an-access-to-information-crisis): Jennifer Chapman on locating information amid government removal and information crisis.
- [The CIA World Factbook, the Access to Information Crisis, and the U.S. Role in the World](https://ripslawlibrarian.wordpress.com/2026/03/04/the-cia-world-factbook-the-access-to-information-crisis-and-the-u-s-role-in-the-world): Jennifer Chapman on CIA World Factbook removal and government information access.

## AI, Technology & Legal Innovation

- [Importance of Not Becoming Too Reliant on Generative AI](https://ripslawlibrarian.wordpress.com/2026/03/18/importance-of-not-becoming-too-reliant-on-generative-ai): Article on risks of over-reliance on ChatGPT and Gemini in legal research.
- [Truth on Trial: Deepfakes and the Future of Evidence](https://ripslawlibrarian.wordpress.com/2026/03/17/truth-on-trial-deepfakes-and-the-future-of-evidence): Article on deepfakes, AI-generated evidence, and implications for legal proceedings.
- [How Dungeons and Dragons Made Me Better at My Job Part 1: Learning New Technologies](https://ripslawlibrarian.wordpress.com/2025/09/15/how-dungeons-and-dragons-made-me-better-at-my-job-part-1-learning-new-technologies): Benjamin Fincher explores how D&D hobby improves legal tech adoption and AI learning.
- [Whither the Index?: Electronic Legal Resources Missing Features Found in Print Counterparts](https://ripslawlibrarian.wordpress.com/2026/03/03/whither-the-index-electronic-legal-resources-missing-features-found-in-print-counterparts): Analysis of missing indexing features in electronic legal resources versus print.

## Information Literacy & Legal Education

- [Guest Post: What is Information Literacy?](https://ripslawlibrarian.wordpress.com/2026/03/09/guest-post-what-is-information-literacy): Part 1: Jamie Aschenbach defines information literacy for law students and research.
- [Guest Post: Tools for Teaching Information Literacy](https://ripslawlibrarian.wordpress.com/2026/03/17/tools-for-teaching-information-literacy): Part 2: Jamie Aschenbach on information literacy teaching tools and TILT framework.

## Professional Development & Librarianship
